u05-rem-early.resolution: Checked every flag; none is a meaning error. Fragment headings (144 Ps 87,6; 145 Ps 87,9b-10a; 146 Ps 87,13 …) are the edition's apparatus; the model repeatedly mistook the next heading for the verse cited (e.g. calling 87:10 wrong because '146 Ps 87,13' follows). Parenthetical John 12:28 / 17:1 / Luke 24:20-21 / 2 Samuel 7:8-9 are identification apparatus for words quoted in the Greek (Ἐδόξασα, Δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν, Παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἄρχοντες …, Ἔλαβόν σε ἐκ τῆς μάνδρας …). 'the fearful judge who is to appear preparing' is right: the genitive absolute τοῦ μέλλοντος ἐπιφανήσεσθαι φοβεροῦ κριτοῦ … προευτρεπίζοντος makes the judge the subject. The rest are particles, participle/finite and imperfect/aorist style.

u05-rem-early.resolution: Not meaning errors. Οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου ἠσθένησαν ἀπὸ πτωχείας is LXX Ps 87:10 (English 88:9); the model's '87:9' is wrong. John 12:28 / 17:1 are apparatus for the quoted Ἐδόξασα and Δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν. ταῦτα ὁ προστάτης … ἐντυγχάνων is elliptical ('these things [says] the champion'); 'This is what … says' supplies the verb the ellipsis implies. ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ κρίσις ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ κρίνεται: God's judgment is passed (judged) by Christ (cf. John 5:22); 'is exercised by Christ' keeps Christ as the judging agent, which is the point of the sentence.
